- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; apply downward bias correction by 1–3% for 30d forecasts.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >+5% from prior 7d mean), model often overshoots and fails to correct; reduce forecast slope by 10–20% in next 7d horizon.
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below 80) after a peak, model overestimates continuation; adjust forecast downward by 2–5% for 30d horizon.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.33) and price is falling, model often underestimates the drop; increase downward bias by 1–3% for 30d horizon.
- If model forecast is flat or rising slowly but true outcome shows sudden drop (e.g., >5% drop in 3d), reduce forecast by 5–10% for next 7d horizon.
- For 30d forecasts, if last 3–5 days of true outcome are below 80 and sentiment is neutral or negative, apply downward bias correction to avoid “false recovery” overfitting.
